_: Department line drawings from the owner's uploads (CERVICAL FASCIA.pdf, GREAT VESSELS OF THE NECK.pdf), mapped to LEARN note sections. Captions are ours. Colour atlas plates copied from published atlases are left out. prepare.py crops them (embedded images, or a y-band of a scanned page for the CNS-levels figures) into ./out (never committed); encrypt.mjs writes the encrypted copies to source/public/dept/ and the manifest to source/public/dept-figs-v16.js.

figs.cap: Deep cervical fascia: a side view, and a cross-section showing the investing, pretracheal and prevertebral layers and the carotid sheath

Veins of the posterior triangle: the external jugular vein and its tributaries
Sternomastoid: its attachments, and its superficial relations (great auricular nerve, transverse cutaneous nerve, external jugular vein, parotid)
Deep relations of the sternomastoid: carotid sheath, lymph nodes, phrenic nerve on scalenus anterior, thyroid lobe, subclavian artery
Muscles deep to the sternomastoid
Cervical plexus: the cutaneous branches, the roots of the ansa cervicalis and the phrenic nerve
Scalene muscles on the 1st and 2nd ribs, with the table of scalenus medius and posterior
Table: the relations and branches of the three parts of the subclavian artery
Subclavian branches: vertebral, internal thoracic and the thyrocervical trunk (inferior thyroid, transverse cervical, suprascapular)
Vertebral artery: its four parts and its relations
Table: the four infrahyoid muscles, their origins and insertions
Great vessels of the head and neck: arch of aorta → brachiocephalic → common carotid → internal and external carotid
Internal carotid artery: its cervical, petrous, cavernous and cerebral parts
Superficial relations of the external carotid: posterior belly of digastric, stylohyoid, hypoglossal nerve, parotid
Deep relations of the external carotid: styloid process with styloglossus and stylopharyngeus, glossopharyngeal nerve, pharyngeal branch of vagus, superior laryngeal nerve, internal carotid
Branches of the external carotid: superficial temporal, maxillary, posterior auricular, occipital, facial, lingual
Facial artery in the neck (A) and in the face (B), with its branches
Internal jugular vein: from the sigmoid sinus at the jugular foramen (superior bulb) to the subclavian vein (inferior bulb), with its tributaries

Table: the relations of the posterior belly of digastric

Relations of hyoglossus: the parts of the lingual artery, the glossopharyngeal nerve and the stylohyoid ligament

Submandibular gland: its position, parts and surfaces
Submandibular duct and the lingual nerve on hyoglossus
Openings of the submandibular and sublingual ducts under the tongue
Relations of the sublingual gland
Submandibular ganglion: chorda tympani through the lingual nerve and sympathetic fibres from the facial artery plexus, to the submandibular and sublingual glands
Styloid apparatus: styloglossus, stylohyoid and stylopharyngeus, with the stylohyoid and stylomandibular ligaments
Table: the three styloid muscles and the two styloid ligaments

Facial nerve: its course from the pons through the internal auditory meatus and the facial canal to the parotid, with its branches

Glossopharyngeal nerve and its branches

CNS level 1 · Spinal cord (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 comma tract (completes reflex arcs) · 2 substantia gelatinosa of Rolando (2nd-order pain & temperature) · 3 dorsal spinocerebellar tract (from Clark's nucleus) · 4 ventral spinothalamic tract (from the main sensory nucleus) · 5 rubrospinal tract (ventral tegmental decussation)

figs.cap: CNS level 2 · Spinal cord (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 comma tract (descending fibres from the cuneate tract) · 2 main sensory nucleus (gives the ventral spinothalamic tract) · 3 lateral spinothalamic tract (continues as the spinal lemniscus) · 4 reticulospinal tract · 5 lateral corticospinal tract (voluntary movement)

figs.cap: CNS level 3 · Spinal cord (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 Lissauer's tract (1st-order pain & temperature) · 2 lateral vestibulospinal tract · 3 sulcomarginal tract (continuation of the MLB) · 4 ventral spinocerebellar tract (both sides of the lower limb) · 5 Clark's nucleus (same side)

figs.cap: CNS level 4 · Spinal cord (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 reticulospinal tract · 2 lateral corticospinal tract · 3 septomarginal (oval) tract (completes reflex arcs) · 4 main sensory nucleus (2nd-order crude touch) · 5 lateral spinothalamic tract (2nd-order pain & temperature)

figs.cap: CNS level 5 · Medulla, motor decussation (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 gracile nucleus (2nd-order proprioception to the cortex) · 2 dorsal spinocerebellar tract (to a subcortical level) · 3 medial longitudinal bundle (continues as the sulcomarginal tract) · 4 rubrospinal tract · 5 pyramidal fibres (upper two-thirds of area 4) crossing in the motor decussation

figs.cap: CNS level 6 · Medulla, sensory decussation (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 internal arcuate fibres (sensory decussation) · 2 spinal nucleus of the trigeminal (axons join the trigeminal lemniscus) · 3 dorsal spinocerebellar tract · 4 medial lemniscus (2nd-order fine touch) · 5 hypoglossal nucleus

figs.cap: CNS level 7 · Pons (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 trigeminal lemniscus (ends in VPMN) · 2 medial lemniscus (ends in VPLN) · 3 medial longitudinal bundle (continues as the sulcomarginal tract) · 4 the bundle keyed as continuing as the septomarginal tract · 5 transverse pontine fibres (separate the pyramidal bundles)

figs.cap: CNS level 8 · Midbrain, inferior colliculus (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncles · 2 trochlear nucleus · 3 inferior colliculus (auditory reflexes) · 4 lateral lemniscus · 5 crus cerebri: pyramidal fibres from the upper two-thirds of area 4

figs.cap: CNS level 9 · Midbrain, superior colliculus (department histology drawing)
figs.ans: Department answers: 1 dorsal tegmental decussation (tectospinal tracts) · 2 red nucleus · 3 oculomotor nucleus · 4 superior colliculus (visual reflexes) · 5 medial lemniscus
